messages:
Maya R: FYI customer ACME hit a big p99 regression after the int8 calibration push last night — p99 from ~450ms -> ~1.3s on /chat.generate. They opened a ticket. I have request_ids and a short repro below.
Toni (support): Thanks — can you paste a request_id and the route/model they hit? Also customer account id so we can scope ACLs.
Maya R: request_id: rq_20260316_93ab, account: acme-inc, route: /v1/chat.generate -> model: redwood-13b-int8-v2. Quant profile used: int8-v2-calib-2026-03-16. Region us-east-1.
Liam K: ops-bot showed increased tail latencies at 22:18 UTC, correlates with the config rollout. Can you attach a quick graph (p95/p99) and if possible a sample input length distribution?
Maya R: attaching inline (small): p95 jumped 2x, p99 ~3x. median unchanged. Seq len median 64 -> 260 for ACME traffic (they started sending longer contexts).
ops-bot: [alert] Route /v1/chat.generate redwood-13b-int8-v2 p99 spike detected at 2026-03-16T22:18Z — +210% over baseline.
Noah (eng-runtime): long context + int8 KV cache layout can rehydrate more frequently and increase compute overhead — but 3x p99 is concerning. Do we have kernel time breakdown?
Maya R: quick flame for rq_20260316_93ab: kernel_cpu: 38ms, dequantize: 420ms, kv_rehydrate: 260ms, I/O wait: 12ms.
Sophia (eng-ml): that dequantize number is huge. It suggests a calibration mismatch where many attention heads require extra pathing, or we hit a slow fallback codepath for certain ops in the int8 kernels. Did we enable fp8 mixed path on that profile?
Liam K: config diff from last week: added `enable_fp8_mixed = true` and updated per-head thresholds in int8-v2-calib. Rollout was a canary -> global at 22:15.
Toni (support): Customer says the regression started exactly after 22:18 and they have SLA complaints. What mitigations can we do right now?
Noah (eng-runtime): short-term options: 1) rollback quant profile to int8-v1 stable, 2) force route to use fp16 variant for ACME, 3) disable fp8 mixed path on the profile (flip a flag). Rolling back the profile is fastest if we can flip config server-side.
Sophia (eng-ml): fallback to fp16 will reduce token throughput but should remove dequantize overhead. Suggest: immediate hotfix -> pin ACME to `redwood-13b-fp16` while we debug int8 profile offline.
Liam K: to pin route for an account: `rictl route update --account acme-inc --route /v1/chat.generate --model redwood-13b-fp16 --sticky true` — that'll take effect within ~30s.
Maya R: doing it now. running the command...
Maya R: done. Customer confirms initial improvement: p99 dropped from ~1.3s -> ~520ms (still a bit higher than baseline).
Toni (support): reply to customer: "We pinned your traffic to fp16 while we investigate the int8 calibration. We'll follow up with timeline for fixing the int8 profile."
Noah (eng-runtime): good quick win. Next: reproduce locally. @Sophia can you run the int8-v2-calib on a long sequence workload and dump per-op timings? Also capture model kernel fallback logs (env RUNTIME_DEBUG=1).
Sophia (eng-ml): on it — I've started a local run with sequences 256/512 and matching tokenization. Early results: when sequence > 256 many attention matmuls hit a fallback path that does per-head dequantize instead of fused path. This explains the 420ms dequantize.
Noah (eng-runtime): OK looks like the int8-kernel selector has a heuristic bug with per-head scales under `int8-v2` for long seqs. Two paths: adjust selector thresholds and ship a targeted kernel patch, or tighten the canary so that long-seq customers don't get int8-v2 until we fix.
Liam K: can we scope a hotfix profile change: set `max_seq_for_int8=256` in int8-v2-calib, and push as emergency config? That would automatically fallback those long requests to fp16 while keeping short seqs on int8.
Sophia (eng-ml): yes, that's lower risk than kernel patch. I'll prepare a profile delta and run calibration sanity. Expect ~15-30m validation.
Maya R: customer's logs show many requests with seq ~300-420. They have a few workflows that spike lengths.
Toni (support): I'll message ACME that we pinned them to fp16 and that we're rolling a profile delta to protect long sequences while we fix kernel. Provide ETA 30-60m.
ops-bot: [deploy] Config change queued: int8-v2-calib -> set max_seq_for_int8=256 (author: sophia). Planned deploy at 2026-03-16T23:10Z to config-store, immediate canary to 1% traffic.
Noah (eng-runtime): request: when the config deploys, add a transient metric (config.protect.longseq) to track how many requests are auto-falling back because of the new threshold. We want to see customer impact.
Sophia (eng-ml): added metric; canary running now. Early telemetry: 7% of traffic hit the fallback rule and their p99 is aligned to fp16. No exceptions thrown.
Liam K: runbook update suggestion: for quant regressions that coincide with seq length shift, prefer profile threshold guard + customer pin to fp16 over immediate global rollback. Less disruptive to other tenants.
Maya R: customer acceptance: ACME says pinned fp16 is acceptable short term, but wants int8 back for cost reasons. We'll keep them in loop.
Toni (support): action items: 1) Sophia validate and deploy profile delta full rollout after 30m canary if green. 2) Noah schedule kernel patch and perf tests (ETA 48h). 3) Liam update runbook note for long-seq guard. 4) Maya coordinate customer comms and postmortem.
Noah (eng-runtime): one more note — add the repro harness (seq=320, batch=1, model=int8-v2) to CI perf so we catch this in future. I'll open PR.
Sophia (eng-ml): will attach per-op timings and diff against int8-v1 in the follow-up ticket.
Maya R: thanks everyone. Marking this thread actioned; I'll close after the postmortem and customer ok. :white_check_mark:
Toni (support): closing loop with ACME now.
ops-bot: [note] Incident tracked in #incidents:INC-2026-032.
